runs.title: Synthetic benchmark (10 images, seed 1)
limitations: Measured on synthetic frames with a simplified PSF/noise model; validates the detector pipeline only, not real-world performance.
Lenient matching (centroid within 3 px) is reported alongside strict IoU>=0.5 AP; point sources are tiny so IoU is a harsh criterion for them.
Both variants share the same seeded images, so the comparison between them is fair; absolute numbers depend on the chosen noise and brightness.

runs.title: Propagation — COSMOS 2251 DEB
limitations: SGP4 with mean elements: positions are typically accurate to ~1 km at epoch and degrade by kilometres per day in LEO (drag, manoeuvres).
Output frame is TEME; latitude/longitude/altitude are derived via GMST and an ellipsoidal Earth for visualisation only.
Image detections cannot be matched to these catalogued objects without calibrated observations (time, pointing, plate solution) and an association step.

runs.title: Close approach — COSMOS 2251 DEB vs COSMOS 2251 DEB
limitations: Preliminary screening estimate from public mean elements (TLE/OMM) propagated with SGP4; not a collision probability and not operational advice.
No covariance is available for TLEs, so probability-of-collision methods (Alfano, Foster, Chan) cannot be applied honestly here.
Miss distances of a few kilometres are within the uncertainty of TLE-based propagation; treat any flagged event as 'needs better data', not as a predicted collision.
Propagation: SGP4/SDP4 (satellite.js 7.x, Vallado 2006 reference implementation); both objects from mean elements (TLE epoch 2026-10-21T06:16:48.277Z, TLE epoch 2026-10-21T03:27:58.309Z).
Frame: TEME (True Equator Mean Equinox) Earth-centred inertial, km / km/s. Separation is the Euclidean norm of the TEME position difference; RIC components are relative to object A.
No manoeuvres, no atmospheric density updates beyond the B* term, no covariance. Typical TLE position errors are ~1 km at epoch, growing with age.
Minimum found by coarse sampling plus golden-section refinement; the result is a preliminary screening estimate, not a collision probability.

runs.title: Tracking — Two moving objects, 8 frames
limitations: Tracks are in IMAGE coordinates (pixels per frame). They are not orbits: converting them needs the plate solution (pixel -> sky direction), accurate exposure timestamps, the observer location and an orbit-determination step.
In sidereal tracking mode stationary tracks are stars; moving tracks are candidate resident space objects (or aircraft/meteors). A motion signature is not an identification.
Greedy nearest-neighbour association can swap identities when trajectories cross; missed detections longer than maxMisses frames split a track.

runs.title: Detection — Bright star field + 2 streaks

metrics.note: Scored against the synthetic ground truth of this sample.

limitations: A detected point source or streak is evidence of a signal on the sensor, not proof of space debris. Stars, satellites, aircraft, meteors and sensor artefacts all produce similar signatures in a single frame.
Confidence is a heuristic function of signal-to-noise ratio, not a calibrated probability.
Classical thresholding struggles with faint sources, crowded fields, blended objects and strong background structure.

runs.title: Detection — Multiple streaks

metrics.note: Scored against the synthetic ground truth of this sample.

limitations: Model trained on StreaksYoloDataset (real data); it only knows the classes streak. Performance on other sensors, exposures or sky conditions is not guaranteed.
A detected streak means a moving object left a trail during the exposure - satellite, debris, aircraft or meteor. Identification requires orbit association, not image analysis.
Confidence scores from a detector trained on a few hundred images are not calibrated probabilities.
